subject: Commit term tradeoffs and SKU tilt — pricing sensitivity to GPU cost (Amethyst AI)
messages:
From: Jamie Liu <jamie@amethyst.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@amethyst.ai
Date: 2026-11-25T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Committed capacity options — sizing + sensitivity to GPU cost

Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood's latency and KV caching. Before we lock in internal approvals I need a clear read on two things so procurement can budget: 1) how you recommend we size reserved capacity (SKU mix) for steady-state vs peak; and 2) how sensitive the committed pricing will be to GPU cost swings.

High level context: we expect steady-state usage roughly 120 vGPU-hours/day in Q1 (inference-heavy reranking + embeddings), with occasional peak bursts to 300 vGPU-hours/day for 2–4 hours. We want to understand the tradeoff between a 3-month pilot commit, 12-month commit (better price), and whether Redwood will absorb GPU cost increases or pass through.

Could you provide a short set of scenarios (3-month vs 12-month, SKU tilt toward cheaper quantized SKUs vs higher perf SKUs) and an explicit statement on discount approvals if GPU market costs move +10% / +20% / -10%? Procurement is particularly sensitive to open-ended pass-through clauses.

Thanks — Jamie
Jamie Liu
Head of Infrastructure
Amethyst AI

Subject: Fwd: Committed capacity options — sizing + sensitivity to GPU cost

Team — forwarding Amethyst's ask. High level proposal below; attaching a scenario workbook (Amethyst_RCP_Scenarios_v1.xlsx) with detailed numbers. Need guidance on discount ceilings and whether we can offer a GPU-cost contingency clause.

Quick proposal (summary):
- Baseline (12-mo commit): 120 vGPU-hrs/day steady, 300 peak bursts. SKU mix: 70% q8_32 (cost-efficient), 30% p6_32 (high perf).
  - List price equivalent: $0.045/token-unit (example unitized), committed discount: 18% off hosted baseline for 12-mo.
- Short pilot (3-mo): smaller commit (50 vGPU-hrs/day), SKU mix more conservative (higher perf), discount: 6% off hosted baseline.

GPU cost sensitivity scenarios (assumptions in sheet):
1) GPU cost down 10%: margin improves — we can hold 18% discount and offer an extra one-time credit (~1-2% equivalent) at renewal.
2) GPU cost flat (baseline): current pricing above holds; discounts as proposed.
3) GPU cost up 10%: falls into two buckets — we can absorb up to ~6% of cost increase via ops optimization and batching; beyond that we need to either reduce discount or trigger a contingency clause.
4) GPU cost up 20%: we cannot absorb — propose a contract clause: price true-up or GPU-cost pass-through capped at +12% annual variance, with customer opt-out window on 60 days' notice.

Decision asks for this thread:
- Approve up to 12% discount without exec sign-off? (we're asking for guidance if a 12% concession is OK)
- If GPU cost increases >10%, can we require a price true-up with a cap at +12%?
- Can we offer a middle ground: a 6-month price true-up window (reduces customer procurement risk) in exchange for 12-mo commit?

Attachments: Amethyst_RCP_Scenarios_v1.xlsx (scenario detail), pricing_terms_draft.docx (draft terms).

Neha
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-26T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Committed capacity options — sizing + sensitivity to GPU cost

Neha — good framing. A couple of product/ops notes and a proposal on the approval ladder: 

- Tying discount movement to a transparent GPU-cost index is the cleanest approach (e.g., public spot/wholesale index + our ops delta). That avoids ad hoc renegotiations. Provide a 6-month lookback to set the index at contract signature.
- For risk appetite: finance can approve up to 10% concession relative to list for customer acquisition (Ben to confirm). Anything >10% should be flagged to VP Sales.
- Suggest a two-way true-up: if GPU cost falls, pass 50% of savings to customer at renewal; if GPU cost rises, allow a capped pass-through (12% annual cap) after 6 months with explicit notice and mitigation options (batching, quantized SKU migration).

Specific ask: include an operational ramp schedule (weeks 1–12) with minimum daily vGPU-hours to protect utilization. If Amethyst wants burst flexibility beyond X hours, we should price bursts at on-demand premium (25% over committed unit).

Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Committed capacity options — sizing + sensitivity to GPU cost

Neha / Karthik — finance take below. Numbers in the attached workbook look reasonable, caveats inline.

- Approval thresholds: finance approves up to 10% effective concession against our target gross margin for standard deals. Approvals >10% need Commercial Director sign-off; >15% require CFO or CRO. Please surface the specific margin impact for the 12% and 18% scenarios in the workbook (I flagged worksheet 'MarginImpact').
- Contingency clause: acceptable to include a GPU-cost index true-up with a +/- lookback and a firm cap at +/-12% annually. We prefer a 90-day notice period but are OK with 60 days if coupled to a 6-month lookback calculation and a maximum of 2 true-ups per 12 months.
- Ramp / utilization: require a minimum utilization floor of 60% of committed vGPU-hours for months 2–6, otherwise a partial true-up to recoup baseline capacity cost. That protects our utilization.

Once you update the workbook with margin deltas and ramp floor language, finance can sign off and we can present to Amethyst.

Ben Carter
Finance — Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference

Jamie / Procurement — thanks for the patience while we hashed internal approvals. Attached is a short proposal and the scenario workbook (Amethyst_RCP_Scenarios_v1.xlsx). High level: 

Offer summary (proposal):
- 12-month reserved capacity: 120 vGPU-hours/day steady state, with burst to 300 vGPU-hours/day priced at on-demand +25%.
- SKU mix: 70% q8_32, 30% p6_32 (can be adjusted quarterly).
- Price: 18% committed discount off hosted list for the 12-month term, subject to the contingency below.

Contingency (GPU-cost sensitivity):
- We propose a transparent GPU-cost index true-up: 6-month lookback to set index at signature; if observed GPU wholesale costs increase more than 10% vs baseline, we will implement a true-up capped at +12% annually.
- If GPU costs decrease, Amethyst receives a 50% share of realized savings applied at renewal.
- True-up mechanics: up to 2 true-ups per 12-month rolling period, 60 days' notice. Finance requires a minimum utilization floor (60% of committed vGPU-hours months 2–6) to keep the committed discount intact.

Next steps:
1) Review the attached workbook for scenario-level numbers (Amethyst_RCP_Scenarios_v1.xlsx).
2) If this structure looks acceptable, I'll push pricing_terms_draft.docx to DocuSign (link included) for signature and provide a 10-day window to finalize.
